top_story: Israel’s 18 November ground push into central Gaza around Bureij and Nuseirat broke the ceasefire’s already frayed credibility, driving displaced families from tents and shelters and exposing how quickly military pressure converts precarious refuge into renewed flight. That escalation followed another night of lethal pressure on Palestinians in the West Bank, where a 72-year-old woman was killed near Jericho during a settler attack and settlers then established an outpost inside Palestinian-administered Area A without prompt Israeli removal. The pattern links battlefield expansion in Gaza with deepening impunity around settler encroachment in the West Bank, shrinking Palestinian civilian space across both arenas. Separately, the US sentencing of a Pakistani man for a plot tied to Qassem Suleimani’s killing underscores how older regional fault lines still reverberate internationally, but the immediate regional reality is one of intensifying insecurity for Palestinians on the ground.
